slides.title: The Effect of Service Quality and Price on Customer Satisfaction in Subsidized Housing at PT Griya Contoh Sejahtera
slides.subtitle: [Name] · [Student ID] · Master of Business Administration · [Defense date]
slides.notes: Good morning, members of the examining committee. Thank you for the opportunity to present my thesis on how service quality and price shape customer satisfaction in subsidized housing.

slides.title: Subsidized housing sales fell 18% in 2025
bullets: Customer complaints centre on two issues:
slides.notes: In 2025 the company's subsidized housing sales dropped by eighteen percent. Complaint records point to two recurring issues: after-sales service and price. This gap motivated the study.

slides.title: Three questions: service, price, and both together
bullets: RQ1: Does service quality affect customer satisfaction?
RQ2: Does price affect customer satisfaction?
RQ3: Do both affect satisfaction simultaneously?
slides.notes: The study asks three questions. The first two test each factor on its own; the third tests them together.

slides.title: Research model: two independent variables, one dependent
slides.notes: Service quality and price are the independent variables; customer satisfaction is the dependent variable. Each arrow corresponds to one research question.

slides.title: Survey of 60 subsidized-home buyers
bullets: Service Quality 4 items, Price 3 items, Satisfaction 3 items
Multiple linear regression, t and F tests, alpha 0.05
slides.notes: I surveyed sixty buyers with a five-point Likert questionnaire and analysed the data with multiple linear regression at a five percent significance level.

slides.title: All three instruments are reliable: Cronbach's alpha 0.788 to 0.847
slides.caption: Source: thesis manuscript, Chapter 4
slides.notes: All three scales exceed the 0.70 threshold, so the instruments are internally consistent.

slides.title: Both service quality and price have positive coefficients
slides.caption: Source: thesis manuscript, Chapter 4. CS = 1.513 + 0.239 SQ + 0.265 P
slides.notes: Both coefficients are positive. Price has a slightly larger coefficient than service quality, which matters for how we read the conclusion.

slides.title: Together, service and price explain 17.5% of satisfaction
slides.caption: Source: thesis manuscript, Chapter 4 (R² = 0.175)
slides.notes: The model explains seventeen and a half percent of the variation in satisfaction. Most of the variation comes from factors outside this model.

slides.title: Recommendation: improve after-sales service
bullets: After-sales complaints appeared in the background data
slides.notes: The practical recommendation is to strengthen after-sales service, which customers already complained about.

slides.title: Conclusion: positive direction, limited explanatory power
bullets: RQ1: service quality coefficient is positive (0.239)
RQ3: together they explain 17.5% of satisfaction
slides.notes: To conclude: both factors point in a positive direction, but together they explain a limited share of satisfaction.

slides.title: Findings hold for one company; wider testing is needed
bullets: Limitation: data from one company, 60 respondents
Future research: other developers and variables
slides.notes: The main limitation is that the data come from a single company. Future studies should include other developers and additional variables.

slides.title: Thank you
slides.notes: Thank you. I welcome your questions and feedback.
